title: Seal the joint between a bath and its tiles, starting from an empty caulking gun
instruction: Seal the joint between the bath and the tiles with an unbroken bead of the silicone, without smearing silicone anywhere else, and leave the gun lying on the table.
context: Resealing the joint between a bath and its tiles is one of the commonest home repairs, done by householders as well as decorators and handymen. Here the gun lies empty beside a new cartridge, so the job includes loading it (its rod comes back only while the release lever is held). What counts is the result, as a householder would judge it: an unbroken bead along the whole joint that wets both the rim and the tiles, no silicone smeared anywhere else, and the gun left lying on the table.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An empty steel skeleton caulking gun for 310 ml cartridges (0.57 kg in all), lying level along the table, nozzle end to the left, its cradle's axis 30 cm forward and 9 cm above the table: a red powder-coated steel frame (0.36 kg) with an open half-round cradle 5.6 cm across and 23.6 cm long, from a back plate 2 cm left of the centre line to a front yoke 25.6 cm left with a V notch for the nozzle; behind the cradle a drive housing 7 cm long, and under its back a black rubber pistol grip 2.4 by 2.8 cm with a flared butt, its foot on the table; the front of the cradle rests on a pine rest block 6 cm wide, 4 cm long and 6 cm tall. (2) The gun's red pressed-steel trigger (70 g), hinged 3 cm below the rod, its 5 cm blade leaning forward in front of the grip with a rounded finger rest 3.6 cm below the pivot, and a return spring (0.10 N m at rest, 0.24 N m fully squeezed, a 36 degree stroke); its short upper arm, 5 mm from the pivot, pushes (3) a steel gripping plate (20 g) on the rod inside the housing, held back by its spring (5 N, 1 N/mm). (4) The gun's zinc-plated steel plunger rod (0.10 kg, 8 mm thick, 30 cm long) with a 4 cm push plate inside the cradle, 8 cm in front of the back plate, and a D-shaped hook (4.4 cm long, 4.4 cm tall, 1 cm wide) at its back end, 20 to 24.4 cm right of the centre line. (5) The gun's zinc-plated steel thumb release lever on top of the housing, its ribbed pad 3 cm wide, 13 cm above the table, between 0.8 cm right and 1.6 cm left of the centre line. (6) A cardboard tray 10 cm wide and 34 cm long, its middle 17 cm forward and 18 cm left, with two notched cardboard saddles; on them, lying along the table with its nozzle to the left, a new 310 ml cartridge of grey sanitary silicone (0.37 kg): a white polyethylene tube 4.9 cm across and 20.5 cm long (bore 4.6 cm) with a blue and yellow label, its polyethylene piston 4 mm in from the back end, and a translucent nozzle 12 cm long, already cut to a 7 mm opening; its middle 17 cm forward and 17.5 cm left. (7) The white acrylic rim of a bath, 10 cm tall, from 14 to 48 cm forward and from 39 to 43.2 cm left, against (8) a wall of white ceramic tiles (7.5 cm square, grey grout) rising 30 cm from 43.2 cm left. The joint to seal is the corner where the rim's top meets the tiles, from 18.5 to 37.7 cm forward (19.2 cm). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Outcomes at the end only: how the gun was loaded, how the trigger was worked, the order of things and where the hands are play no part. The gun works as a real smooth-rod gun: squeezing the trigger toward the grip pushes the gripping plate forward (10:1 at 5 cm below the trigger's pivot), and the plate carries the rod forward; let go, the plate slides back along the rod. The rod slides in freely but comes back out only while the release lever is pressed down at least 6 degrees. The rod's push plate pushes the cartridge's piston, which the silicone resists with 150 N, so no sealant comes without the cartridge loaded and the trigger squeezed. Sealant: the piston's advance times the 46 mm bore (1.66 ml per mm) leaves the nozzle's tip 0.25 s later and is laid along the tip's path. Where the bead it makes touches both the rim's top and the tiles (the tip within the bead's radius plus 2 mm of each surface) it is in the joint, shared over the joint's 1 mm lengths it covers; a 1 mm length is sealed when it holds at least 12.6 mm2 (a bead at least 4 mm across; a 6 mm bead is 28.3 mm2). Sealant laid with the tip more than 1 cm from the tiles or from the rim's top, or beyond the bath's ends, is mess. At the end: 1.0 if at least 95% of the joint is sealed with no unsealed stretch longer than 2 mm (its ends included), at most 0.1 ml of mess, and the gun lying on the table (its grip's foot within 2 cm of the table top, tilted at most 25 degrees); 0.75 if sealed and clean so but the gun not lying on the table; 0.5 if at least 50% of the joint is sealed; 0.25 if at least 25% of it is sealed; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the gun, its trigger, gripping plate, rod and lever, the cartridge and its piston still. In a real trial: photograph the joint from above with a steel rule along it; the sealed length is where the bead is at least 4 mm wide and wets both the rim and the tile, read off the rule to the millimetre, as is the longest gap (sealed fraction = sealed length / 192 mm); mess is all silicone more than 1 cm from the corner (on the tiles, the bath, the table), scraped onto foil and weighed on a 0.01 g scale: sanitary silicones are 0.98 to 1.05 g/ml, so 0.1 ml is about 0.1 g; whether the gun lies on the table on its grip is read from the same photograph.
reset_notes: Scrape the bead and any mess off the bath, tiles and table, take the cartridge out of the gun and lay a new one on the tray, press the release and set the rod with its plate 8 cm in front of the back plate, and lay the gun back on its grip and rest block.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). Physical: sprung hinged trigger (10:1), sprung gripping plate, rod, piston. Rules: the plates' friction grip on the smooth rod (a one-way stop kept behind the gripping plate; a hold on the rod unless the lever is down) and the silicone's 150 N resistance (a capped spring moved along the piston). Silicone is not simulated: piston advance x 16.6 cm2 leaves the tip 0.25 s later, laid where the tip is. Grip 9 cm long (real about 12).
